subject: VeloxAI: sudden hosted API latency & error surge - escalation
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma.carter@veloxai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@veloxai.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency & 500 surge on Hosted API - impacting production

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a dramatic rise in p95/p99 latency and an increase in 5xx errors against our production routes hitting your Hosted API around 07:45 PT this morning. Impact: several customer-facing features are timing out (~30s) and our error rate jumped from 0.2% to ~6% in the last 30 minutes.

Host: velox-models-prod (using redwood hosted, model: redwood/llama-13b-quant-v2)
Observed: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~1.8s (was 220ms), p99 ~6.2s (was 420ms).
Errors: 500/timeout spikes correlated with higher request concurrency.

Attached a small sample of errors and an example request/trace: server-oom-20260709.log (excerpt).

This is causing immediate customer outages for two of our largest accounts. Can you triage urgently?

Thanks,
Emma Carter
Head of AI Operations, VeloxAI
[attachment: server-oom-20260709.log (text/plain)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@veloxai.com>
Cc: Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@veloxai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & 500 surge on Hosted API - impacting production

Emma — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra/serving team now (cc: Rishi). Immediate plan:

- We’ll open a dedicated incident and share a private status link within 15 minutes.
- I’ll propose mitigations you can enable from your side (concurrency cap, shorter max_tokens) while we stabilize.
- Can you confirm if you pinned to a specific model version or using auto model selection? Also send the HubSpot customer IDs so I can link the case.

We’ll push updates as soon as we have a postmortem vector. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize this.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Carter <emma.carter@veloxai.com>, Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@veloxai.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: URGENT: VeloxAI p99 spike — possible GPU OOMs (customer-impacting)

Team — VeloxAI is reporting a customer-impacting spike in p95/p99 latency and error rate on hosted routes. They attached server OOM log excerpts. Impacting production for multiple customers.

Customer context:
- Account: VeloxAI (large-scale inference, multi-tenant usage)
- Model: redwood/llama-13b-quant-v2 (appears to be an optimized quantized variant)
- Start: ~07:45 PT 2026-07-09
- Symptoms: p99 latency jump to ~6s; retriable 500s and occasional OOM traces in the logs.

Immediate asks: can infra/serving run a headroom check and confirm whether any recent runtime changes (quantization kernel updates, memory allocator tweaks) were rolled out to hosted fleet in the last 48h? Marcus, pls surface any autoscaler anomalies. Laura/Rishi — we need a triage channel, logs and a proposed short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact.

Attachments: server-oom-20260709.log (customer), kv-eviction-sample.json (customer-captured).

—Kim

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Carter <emma.carter@veloxai.com>, Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@veloxai.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: VeloxAI p99 spike — possible GPU OOMs (customer-impacting)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- We’ve reproduced similar symptoms in the hosted fleet logs: short bursts of GPU memory fragmentation leading to OOMs on some inference workers serving this quantized model. The runtime is seeing many small allocation/free patterns from KV cache churn + recent kernel selection heuristics for the quantized path.
- Fragmentation causes one worker to OOM and drop requests; the router retries/fallbacks increase tail latency (p99) and can amplify queueing on other workers.
- We did a behind-the-scenes rollback of a quantization kernel heuristic deployed yesterday and increased per-instance memory headroom on a subset of affected pools — this reduced immediate OOM counts in telemetry.

Immediate mitigations (already in progress):
1) Rollback quant kernel heuristic (done for affected pool).
2) Temporarily increase instance headroom + lower worker concurrency limit for the model family (done, rolling).
3) Disable aggressive KV prefix caching for VeloxAI routes (opt-out) to reduce small alloc/free churn (in progress).
4) Recommend Velox pin to redwood/llama-13b-quant-v1 (less aggressive quant) as a customer-side mitigation.

Next steps:
- We will keep the incident open and collect full heap/alloc traces; Rishi will own the postmortem.
- Laura and Marcus will run capacity increases and confirm autoscaler health.
- I’ll provide a concise customer-facing note for Kimberly to send with immediate steps we recommend.

We’ll aim for a 1-hr update.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
[rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai]
[attachment: redwood-debug-dump-20260709.tar.gz (partial)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@veloxai.com>, Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@veloxai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & 500 surge on Hosted API - escalation and mitigations

Emma / Daniel — short customer note and immediate actions you can take now to reduce impact:

1) Pin to model: redwood/llama-13b-quant-v1 (we recommend this variant for now).
2) Apply a client-side concurrency cap of 8 for this route and reduce max_tokens by 25% temporarily.
3) If you can, set request timeout to 6s to fail fast and avoid long queueing that increases downstream p99.

What we’ve done on our side: rolled back a quant kernel heuristic; increased instance headroom; throttled worker concurrency in affected pools; disabling aggressive KV prefix caching for your routes (to reduce fragmentation).

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260709-VX
We’re keeping an incident bridge open and will share a 1-hr update. I’ve also asked for a service credit evaluation given customer impact — I’ll confirm by EOD.

Apologies again — we’re treating this as priority one. If you’re available we can do a quick 30-min sync at 10:00 PT.

—Kim

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Carter <emma.carter@veloxai.com>, Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@veloxai.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & action items — VeloxAI p99 regression (root cause: GPU memory fragmentation / KV churn)

Team / Velox AI — final summary and action plan:

Summary:
- Root cause: memory fragmentation in the quantized execution path exacerbated by heavy KV cache churn. Small allocation/free patterns (many short-lived KV entries) led to allocator fragmentation on GPUs and intermittent OOMs on workers serving the quantized kernel. When a worker OOMs, router retries and fallback behavior contributed to p99 amplification.
- Timeline: issue onset 2026-07-09 07:45 PT; mitigation rollbacks and capacity adjustments reduced OOM frequency by ~85% within 45 minutes; full stabilization by 12:00 PT after targeted pool scaling.

Immediate actions completed:
- Reverted quant kernel heuristic from 2026-07-08 deploy.
- Increased per-instance memory headroom for affected pools.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive KV prefix caching and set a conservative eviction policy for VeloxAI routes.
- Applied short-term worker concurrency caps.
- Customer guidance delivered (model pin, concurrency cap, timeout) and incident bridge held.

Planned follow-up (owner / ETA):
- Deep allocator heap analysis + allocator patch (Rishi) — ETA 2 weeks.
- Improved KV cache GC throttling to avoid bursty small alloc/free (Marcus) — ETA 10 days.
- Test harness for quantized kernel fragmentation scenarios (Laura) — ETA 3 weeks.
- Postmortem and customer credit proposal (Kimberly) — ETA 3 business days.

Attachments: action-plan-veloxai-20260711.pdf (contains timeline, telemetry, and remediation details).

If Velox wants an executive sync, please propose times and we’ll escalate to our leadership. We’ve also flagged this for priority scheduling in the serving roadmap.

—Rishi Malhotra
VP, Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
